promotion_note: PROMOTED 2026-07-30 (nyiso-100 session; owner instruction in-session: 'if structural integrity improves but gates regress that may still be a keeper'). NYISO keeper -> 2026-07-30-nyiso-100-silretire (bundle results/calibration/nyiso100_silretire, DETERMINATION NOT-YET — C3c remains the SOLE blocker, the same determination class as every prior NYISO keeper). ONE delta vs the nyiso-99 keeper: nyiso_import_sil_retire. THE SESSION'S PRIMARY RESULT IS AN IDENTIFICATION, AND IT IS A PROVENANCE RESULT, NOT A NEW NUMBER. The nyiso-99 charter carried this forward as 'a hand-set estimate measurement contradicts'; that framing was TOO GENEROUS. The 4,350 MW NYISO_simultaneous_import cap is a REAL published NYISO quantity measured on the WRONG BOUNDARY: it is EXACTLY the G-J LOCALITY Bulk Power Transmission Limit for capability year 2024/2025 (data/raw/capacity-deliverability/nyiso/nyiso.csv, area 'G-J', import_limit; 2024-25 Locality Bulk Power Transmission Capability Report p.7) — an INTERNAL New York transfer boundary (Load Zones G,H,I,J) — installed as the EXTERNAL NYCA simultaneous-import cap. THREE CORROBORATIONS it is mis-attribution, not coincidence: (a) exactly ONE row in the entire published import_limit table equals the constant and it is the G-J row, while the published G-J series MOVES by capability year (3,425 / 3,425 / 4,350 / 4,500 for 2022/23-2025/26) and the constant is frozen at the 2024/25 reading across all three solve years — including 2023, whose own value is 3,425; (b) the constant's OWN justification comment argued from INTERNAL downstate interfaces ('Dunwoodie-South 3.9 GW into NYC, cable-limited 1.65 GW into LI') — an internal-boundary rationale attached to an external limit — and its border-link arithmetic OMITTED the Capital_Hudson link entirely (it summed 5.2 GW against a real 6.8 GW); (c) THE CITED SOURCE DOES NOT CONTAIN IT — extraction over all three 2023-2025 Gold Books on disk finds ZERO pages naming a simultaneous import or transfer limit, and Table VI-1 is REDACTED as Critical Energy Infrastructure Information in every edition, so NYISO publishes no aggregate external simultaneous import limit available to this repo at all. MEASUREMENT FALSIFIES IT AS AN EXTERNAL BOUND: NYCA net import reached 5,929/5,662/5,872 MW metered (EIA-930) and 7,078/7,298/6,727 MW scheduled (NYISO MIS P-32), exceeding 4,350 MW in 287/314/145 h and 865/685/388 h — and the P-32 sum is cross-validated as NYCA net interchange rather than a double-count of the three HQ rows (UTC-joined r 0.910/0.906/0.879, bias +17/-179/-262 MW on means of 2,677/2,322/2,612 MW; a double-count would bias ~+1,200 MW). WHY IT RETIRES RATHER THAN RAISES (the hard part was identification, not the edit): the naive measured replacement — the sum of posted per-interface P-32 limits, 10,575/10,715/10,450 MW — is PRECISELY rule 14's named misalignment exception, several parallel paths this five-zone network collapses into one link, and there is no published external limit to substitute. But the misalignment does NOT extend to every path: for the two links whose tie sets are point-to-point HVDC converters there is no parallel-path ambiguity at all and the model is ALREADY at the posted rating (NYC 1,000 vs HTP 660 + Linden-VFT 315 = 975 posted; Long_Island 1,200 vs Neptune 660 + Cross-Sound 330 + NPX-1385 200 = 1,190 posted), with the AC seams behind the internal Central-East chain the topology already carries (2,850 MW model vs a P-32 CENTRAL EAST - VC posted median 2,865 MW). Retiring introduces NO new number and REMOVES a free parameter: the aggregate becomes the border-link sum 6,800 MW, INSIDE the measured admissible interval [5,929 lower bound, 10,715 posted-rating upper bound], where 4,350 lay OUTSIDE it in all three years. Rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH] reinforces it — shared-upstream-capacity limitation already has a mechanism here (the internal interface chain); the scalar was a second one pointed at the wrong boundary. RULE-24 SIDE EFFECT: the retired constant was solve-affecting but carried NO DOF ledger entry, so the retire also closes a registry gap. n_residual STAYS 6 on a UNION'd 24-entry ledger (gen_nyiso100_attestation.py). A/B, EVERY PRE-REGISTERED GATE PASSES (PREREG committed AND PUSHED pre-solve; replay_keeper.py on the keeper's own meta.json, so the flag is the only delta): G0 a SEPARATE same-HEAD zero-delta control (2026-07-29-nyiso-100-control-zerodelta) reproduces the nyiso-99 keeper BIT-FOR-BIT in all three years — max |delta class MW| 0.000000, max |delta price| 0.000000 $/MWh; G1 LIVE-mechanism (nyiso-89 §4a) — arm topology carries ZERO import-node interface limits, control exactly one at 4,350 MW, confirmed by topology rebuild AND the arm's own solve log; G2 import max 4,350.0 -> 6,518.9/6,470.0/6,075.0 MW with hours pinned AT the old cap 548/689/176 -> 0/2/0 and hours above it 0 -> 436/587/161, every maximum inside the pre-registered (4,350, 6,800] window; G3 the +-2% monthly reconciliation band HOLDS in every month of every year and months at the upper edge RISE 10/11/11 -> 12/12/11, so the arm reallocates a band-bounded quota rather than escaping it (import energy moves only +0.041/+0.070/+0.035 TWh = +0.17/+0.34/+0.18 %); G4 C1 all 14/14 · free 10/10, IDENTICAL to the keeper, with the knife-edge 2023 CC_REGULAR cell still passing — the ISO's tightest, and it DOES move under this delta: -2.79 of ±2.94 in the control (32.512 TWh, the prior keeper's own value) -> -2.80 in the arm (32.497 TWh), a ~15 GWh/yr CC_REGULAR shift, still comfortably inside band; G5 C7 PASS and C8 PASS — the fragile 2024 ST_GAS grounded-above-budget cell moves 30.4 -> 30.6 % forced, i.e. slightly further above the cap, but stays a GROUNDED pass and its grounding evidence IMPROVES on BOTH legs (D-1 profile r 0.954 -> 0.958, off-peak CV ratio 0.957 -> 0.972) with every binding mechanism still clearing D-4. SLACK AND DUMP STAY EXACTLY 0.0 MWh in every year, both runs. REPORTED, NOT CLAIMED, AND NOT USED TO JUSTIFY ANYTHING (rule 1 [R-STRUCT], both directions): G6 C3c h>$300 4/0/7 -> 3/0/7 vs actual 10/12/42 and mean LMP 33.56/36.32/58.98 -> 33.49/36.22/58.95 — the PRE-REGISTRATION PREDICTED C3c WOULD TICK UP and it ticked DOWN, because volume was not in fact fixed (reaching the band ceiling in two more months added ~0.15 TWh); THAT PREDICTION IS RECORDED AS WRONG rather than re-narrated. G7 import r_hr 0.598/0.623/0.453 -> 0.584/0.605/0.451, worse in all three years — exactly as pre-registered and for the reason given: the retired cap was binding 54/59/62 % OVERNIGHT (h21-h03) and only 3/2/2 % in h16-h18, and in 84/89/94 % of cap-bound hours the REAL system imported LESS than the cap, so the cap was flattering the statistic by truncating the model in hours reality was quieter. Item 9 is CLOSED as an attributed C3c symptom (nyiso-99, matrix import_shape_lever -> G) and the import node is EXONERATED, so a worse r_hr is not evidence against this arm. FOLLOW-ON LEVER, DELIBERATELY NOT ARMED (single-delta discipline): the G-J locality limit is a REAL constraint the topology does not represent AT ITS OWN BOUNDARY; it belongs on the INTERNAL G-J interface in the nyiso_nyc_lcr_tsl / nyiso_li_lcr_tsl family, and owes its own rule-14 boundary reconciliation first (the five-zone aggregation has no clean G-J cutset: G sits in Capital_Hudson, H+I in Lower_Hudson, J is NYC). Matrix row nyiso_import_sil_retire -> K. PRE-EXISTING AND UNCHANGED, INHERITED NOT CAUSED: D-5 parity FAILs on nyiso_local_selfsupply, identical to the nyiso-99 keeper's and this session's control. THE CAVEAT IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE BENCHMARK IS WRONG: the measured RT tail is real (model 3/0/7 h vs actual 10/12/42 h >$300) and the model under-produces it. It records an EXHAUSTED lever queue on a diagnosed structural limitation of the five-zone representation — items 1/1b refused ex-ante on identification (nyiso-94/95), item 5 inert ex-ante (nyiso-93), items 2/3 closed and tested (nyiso-96), the last surviving candidate SCUC load-pocket security commitment + BPCG closed ex-ante on CONTENT not merely access (nyiso-97), import shape refused as an attributed C3c symptom with the seam exonerated (nyiso-99), G-J locality refused ex-ante for want of a representable boundary (nyiso-101). The one nominally-open item (nyiso_iroquois_winter_spread) is blocked on a joint SUMMER scarcity lever, and summer is exactly what is exhausted — nyiso-92 dated the actual RT tail as summer (2025 Jun 23-25 alone = 18 of 42 h; the Jan-2024 storm produced ZERO >$300 hours), capping the winter-fuel lane at ~4-5 h/yr. Rule 1 [R-STRUCT] is why this is a ledger entry and not a mechanism: every remaining way to lift the tail is fitted to the tail residual.
